title: Review seats run no programs
summary: A review seat can no longer run a program on your machine: codex seats get a closed tool set and every seat order says what the seat may run.

caps/test-too-small.why: Whether a few test lines are worth a follow-up is a call about how much risk you carry, and only you can make it.
caps/test-too-small.context: The test for the list and search size caps uses too little data to ever hit a cap, so it would still pass if those caps were removed.

items.title: Codex review seats no longer see your codex config
items.ifLeft: A review that relied on a custom codex MCP server, plugin, hook or model-provider setting loses it.

items.title: Cursor review seats can still run commands; they are caught afterwards
items.ifLeft: A cursor seat that runs a command forfeits its review, but the command will already have run inside cursor's sandbox.

items.title: A codex or cursor review attempt that dies mid-run forfeits for good
items.ifLeft: You may see a few more reviewer fallbacks to the host model when a seat crashes; each one is disclosed.

items.title: What you're accepting
ifLeft: A seat whose record has a line over 1 MiB, or runs past 64 MiB, forfeits and the fallback is disclosed.
A line past 2,000 characters takes several reads; the seat gets the first 2,000 characters and a note to read on.
The PR is larger than estimated, and the advisor ruled to continue as one PR, for your veto.
This leg's fixer broke one order rule once; the content was reviewed and audited like any other fix.
